allOf.description: Inherits shared step-base properties ($schema, id, owner, created_at, canonical_refs_used).

extension_decision.description: Records the explicit decision on whether domain-specific extensions are needed. Required on every step 13 artifact — forces the author to evaluate and justify rather than silently omitting extensions.

status.description: Whether the project requires domain-specific extensions. 'extensions-required' when at least one domain needs ≥3 dedicated schema sections not expressible in core steps. 'none-required' when all domains are adequately covered by core steps 05-07.

rationale.description: Justification for the decision. For 'none-required', must cite component_ids from 02_system_sketch.json AND NFR categories from 07_nfrs.json evaluated and ruled out. For 'extensions-required', must cite the specific domain gaps that necessitate extensions.

extensions.description: Ordered list of domain-specific extension specs to generate as part of this step. Each entry defines one extension artifact (its ID, schema requirements, and governance anchors). When extension_decision.status is 'none-required', this array must be empty.

extension_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this extension, scoped to the project. Format: ext-{NN}-{topic} where NN is a zero-padded sequence number and topic is a short descriptor. Examples: 'ext-01-database', 'ext-02-auth-provider', 'ext-03-payment-gateway'. Should be stable once assigned — renaming breaks downstream traceability. Avoid generic names like 'ext-01-misc'.

title.description: Short, human-readable name for this extension displayed in reports and the trace matrix. Should be title-cased and describe the domain concern clearly (e.g. 'Database Layer Extension', 'Authentication Provider Extension'). Avoid abbreviations.

area_of_concern.description: High-level domain category this extension addresses. Use a concise noun phrase that classifies the extension's technical scope. Decision rule: when two area names could apply, choose the one that describes the domain concern (the business problem being extended), not the technology implementing it. Canonical disambiguation: 'AI' for user-facing AI features such as recommendation engines, content generation, and AI assistants; 'ML' for model training pipelines, experimentation frameworks, and model management infrastructure; 'Payments' for payment processing flows, transaction management, and financial reconciliation; 'Data' for ETL pipelines, analytics schemas, and data quality frameworks. Examples: an LLM-powered chat feature → 'AI'; a model retraining pipeline → 'ML'; a Stripe integration → 'Payments'; a dbt pipeline → 'Data'. Other accepted values: 'Security', 'Notifications', 'Infrastructure'. Anti-pattern: 'General', 'Other', 'Misc' — these defeat the purpose of domain-specific extensions and will be flagged by canonical-lint; every extension must have a specific, nameable concern.

justification.description: Rationale explaining why this extension is necessary and why it could not be covered by the core spec steps. Should reference the specific gap, risk, or domain need. A weak justification ('it is needed') is insufficient — cite the driving functional requirement, NFR, or governance rule. Minimum one substantive sentence.

required_schema_sections.description: Schema sections that must be present in any valid extension generated by this template. Each entry identifies a mandatory structural element. Use to enforce non-negotiable quality gates — for example, every extension should have a 'trace' section and a 'validation_rules' section. Extensions that omit required sections fail the extension generator validation. Must contain at least the sections that establish traceability and governance for the extension.

items.description: Exact key name of a section that must appear in the generated extension schema. Use the exact JSON key as it will appear in the schema's properties. Common sections by area_of_concern: for 'Data' → 'entities', 'schemas', 'migrations'; for 'Security' → 'policies', 'threat_models', 'access_controls'; for 'Payments' → 'providers', 'transaction_types', 'reconciliation'; for 'AI/ML' → 'models', 'evaluation_criteria', 'data_lineage'. Always include 'trace' and 'validation_rules' as minimum sections regardless of area_of_concern. Anti-pattern: 'general', 'other', 'misc' — every section name should be domain-specific.

schema_design_guidelines.description: Prose guidance for the AI or author generating this extension's JSON schema. Must contain at least one verification keyword (verif, test, check, validat, assert). Must specify: (1) which canonical $defs from schema/core/ must be reused rather than redefined, (2) any ID format patterns for objects within the extension, (3) structural constraints unique to this domain, and (4) what to avoid. Decision rule: guidelines are sufficient when any reviewer could implement the schema without making structural choices — if a guideline leaves the implementer guessing, it is too vague. Example for 'Payments': '(1) reuse vc:core:atoms#httpMethod for method fields rather than redefining; (2) all payment entry IDs follow pay-{noun}-{n} pattern; (3) every payment entry must include currency_code (ISO 4217 three-letter code) and amount_cents (non-negative integer); (4) avoid hardcoding currency symbols in enum values — use codes only.' Example for 'Security': '(1) reuse vc:core:atoms#severityLevel for risk fields; (2) all control IDs follow ctrl-{category}-{n}; (3) every control must include enforcement_layer from the approved enum.' Anti-pattern: generic guidelines like 'follow good naming conventions' that do not specify which atoms to reuse or what structural constraints apply — these provide no actionable constraint and will be silently ignored by generators.

tag_ref.description: Canonical reference to a tag that categorises this extension. Kind is structurally pinned to 'tag'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:tag:critical-path", "kind": "tag"}. Used by canonical-lint to validate that extension tags resolve to known categories. Define the tag in canon/manifest.json before referencing it here.

policy_ref.description: Canonical reference to the governance policy that applies to this extension. Kind is structurally pinned to 'policy'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:policy:spec-first", "kind": "policy"}. Reference when the extension area has a specific compliance framework or organisational policy governing it.

id_pattern_ref.description: Canonical reference to the ID naming pattern used for items in this extension. Kind is structurally pinned to 'id_pattern'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:id_pattern:conventional-commit", "kind": "id_pattern"}. Include only when the extension schema uses a non-standard ID pattern. Omit when IDs follow the standard kebab-case pattern enforced by vc:core:atoms#kebabId.

governance_label_ref.description: Canonical reference to the governance label applied to this extension. Kind is structurally pinned to 'governance_label'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:governance_label:mandatory", "kind": "governance_label"}. Required field — dual-checked by canonical-integrity (canon/manifest.json) and step_13.py (10_governance.json canonical_refs_used). Links the extension to its governance review tier (mandatory, recommended, optional).

items.description: A single extension spec definition. Bundles the extension's identity (extension_id, title), domain scope (area_of_concern), rationale (justification), structural requirements (required_schema_sections, schema_design_guidelines), and canonical registry anchors (tag_ref, policy_ref, id_pattern_ref, governance_label_ref). Output filename is derived: extension_id with hyphens replaced by underscores + '.json'.

extension_decision.description: Conditional: when status is none-required, extensions must be empty.

status.description: Matches none-required status for conditional enforcement.

extensions.description: Enforced empty when extension_decision.status is none-required.

extension_decision.description: Conditional: when status is extensions-required, extensions must be non-empty.

status.description: Matches extensions-required status for conditional enforcement.

extensions.description: Enforced non-empty when extension_decision.status is extensions-required.
